criteria.criterion: Compactor tolerates what readers bless: a zero-byte or unparseable folder row (not one JSON object) is dropped from the closed day's folder with a record (moved to ccmorph/usage-dropped/<day>/<mtime_ns>-<name> plus one stderr line), so the day still compacts and its folder closes; a multiline receipt, which readers count, stays in the folder; identity conflicts keep both rows as readers do; CompactUsage skips a failing day and continues; an orphan idx is healed on first sight. Check: `go test ./shim -run 'TestCompactUsageToleratesReaderBlessedStates|TestCompactUsageBadDayDoesNotBlockNewerDays|TestCompactUsageKilledPublicationHealsOnNextRead'` (the subtest 'uncountable row is dropped with a record' asserts the folder is gone and usage-dropped/2026-11-14/20-bad.json holds the exact bytes), `go test ./quota -run TestQuotaSpendIndexOnlyOrphanAnswersFromFolder`, and tests/usage_shard_export_test.py::test_index_only_orphan_answers_from_the_folder. A same-name multiline overlay over an existing archive leaves the archive and index bytes and the live bytes untouched (subtest 'multiline overlay keeps its archived twin').

criteria.criterion: Transient/foreign damage degrades, never bricks, and never hangs: the report skips an unreadable file and continues (the pre-#537 reading): with a receipt still there but unreadable (mode 0, or a FIFO under a receipt's name) `ccmorph-core shim report` exits 0, prints the total of every other row and a line `not readable N receipt(s), skipped: cost unknown; check their permissions`, and names each skipped receipt on stderr; a receipt gone between listing and read is skipped by report, quota and export alike; every store read opens through paths.OpenRegular / the export's read_regular, so no reader or compactor waits on a FIFO; archivedDayRows falls back to the hash-verified archive when the leftover folder is unreadable; the hook cursor pins only on the row's own write/lock failure; an unopenable store lock is read past, never unlinked, in Go and in share/usage-export. Check: `go test ./util/paths ./shim ./quota -run 'TestReadRegularFileRefusesAFIFOWithoutWaiting|TestReportNamesAnUnreadableRowFile|TestCompactUsageNeverWaitsOnAFIFO|TestQuotaSpendUnreadableLeftoverFolderAnswersFromArchive|TestTranscriptRecordIgnoresForeignArchiveDamage|Lock' -v` all PASS (TestReportNamesAnUnreadableRowFile asserts exit 0, `total spend $7.00`, `not readable 2 receipt(s), skipped`, and both names on stderr), plus tests/usage_shard_export_test.py's two lock tests (test_export_reads_past_an_unopenable_move_lock_and_keeps_it, test_export_reads_without_a_lock_when_the_lock_is_stuck).
criteria.evidence: The criterion's go test run: util/paths, shim and quota ok, 14 --- PASS, no FAIL. TestReportNamesAnUnreadableRowFile now asserts exit 0, `total spend $7.00`, `not readable 2 receipt(s), skipped` and both names on stderr. Both usage_shard_export lock tests passed. The report reads flat rows first (move ordering, #537) but counts them after the day folders, so a response under both names counts by its day copy, as quota and the export do.

criteria.criterion: One merge rule for all three readers: the same-name/non-finite identity decision is one Go helper shared by quota and shim (paths.SameNamedRows, the archive sentinel named once as paths.ArchiveCopySuffix), the export normalizes non-finite the same way, and a NaN-cost row later rewritten in the live folder yields identical totals in quota, report and export. Check: `go test ./quota ./shim -run 'TestQuotaSpendNonFiniteOverlayUnpricesNotOmits|TestReportNonFiniteOverlayCountsUnknownNotDollars'` and tests/usage_shard_export_test.py::test_nonfinite_overlay_is_one_turn_priced_as_written.

share/usage-export parses each receipt inside export()'s loop: one truncated overlay row is skipped and the rest of the year still exports. Check: tests/usage_shard_export_test.py::test_a_truncated_overlay_skips_and_the_rest_of_the_year_exports.

Clock-window fixes: the open/closed boundary is computed once per pass from the same instant readers and the compactor share (paths.UsageOpenFrom); openMarks consults the archive for days >= openFrom; auto-compaction never compacts a day any reader can still classify open; and the redirect re-stamp re-takes the target day's closed lock. Check: `go test ./quota ./shim -run 'TestQuotaSpendClockStepForwardThenBackKeepsTheMonthWhole|TestAClockRewindRedirectWaitsForTheTargetDaysLock'`.

No unbounded blocks on hot paths (INTENT 8): quota reads, hook writes and the export take bounded locks or refuse with 'usage store busy'; the memo Mutex is not held across archive I/O; quota's own maintenance is shim.CompactUsageWithin with a 500 ms deadline, a 2000-entry cap and a 2 MiB byte cap (archive+index by stat, folder receipts as read, each open non-blocking), so a read that wins the store lock never reads or rewrites a day without a bound.
